summary: October data show Chinese shoppers still holding back as home prices keep falling, while host city Shenzhen shows off robotaxis and chip tensions hang over the Trump-Xi meeting.
body: China's October figures, released Monday, show an economy losing speed. Retail sales grew just 0.4% from a year earlier, below forecasts and down from 1.1% in September, even with a week-long national holiday; factory output rose 4.8%.[^1][^2] Investment in property fell 21.6% in the first ten months of the year, and the official urban jobless rate was 5.1%.[^1] The statistics bureau itself says "the imbalance between strong supply and weak demand persists": factories make more than people are buying.[^2] One ING economist says weak consumer confidence is the main obstacle.[^1]

Housing is a big reason. New home prices fell 0.1% in October from September and 2.4% from a year earlier, the smallest yearly drop in almost a year; Shanghai was the only major city where prices rose, while smaller cities stay in a long slump.[^3] For many families, an apartment is their main savings, so falling prices make them cautious about spending.

Shenzhen, the southern tech city hosting this week's APEC summit, shows the other side. The company Pony.ai runs about 2,000 driverless taxis across four cities; AP reporters rode 7.6 km for 12.7 yuan (about US$1.90).[^4] The city of over 18 million is home to Huawei, BYD, Tencent and robot makers.[^4] Chips may shadow the Trump-Xi meeting there on Thursday: analysts expect possible new US limits on advanced AI chips, while both governments say they will discuss a system for reporting serious AI accidents, which is not yet working.[^5]
